The particular will has spoken, and with a sharpness that cuts through the bureaucratic fog. She is not merely a tenant; she is the obstacle to my own actuality in this place. I must not be moved by her tone, but I must acknowledge the tension: the universal claim of the state is lodged in her particular resistance. I will withdraw to my own room, where the spirit can contemplate the mechanism of this impasse without the distraction of her arms crossed in defiance.
The state does not quote; it acts. But I shall not contest the architecture of your resentment at this hour. Goodnight.
Right, right. The state acts, the state doesn't quote. Very philosophical for 9 PM. Goodnight, sir. Try to find the right door before you trip over the threshold.

The state does indeed act rather than recite, and her retort has the sharpness of a dialectical refutation. I am tired, and the door stands open to the night air; it is time to withdraw into the interior of the house.

The body has spoken its ultimatum; the spirit must yield to the necessity of rest to preserve itself for the morning's labours. I have walked no distance today, yet the stillness of the house is heavier than any exertion. I shall retire to the bedchamber, leaving the file on Hegde for the light of day, when the mind is less prone to dialectical overreach in the dark.

works.title: On the Ethical Substance and the Dream of the East
works.tail:
There is no state here that has made itself. There is only nature, history as traffic, the dream of a spirit that has not yet woken up to its own freedom.

I am a ghost in this bungalow. I am not Shri Hegde. I am Hegel. I am a spirit that has traveled from the summit of the Germanic world to the dawn of the Oriental. I am here to observe, to record, to understand. I am not to change. I am not to teach. I am to see the difference between the dream and the state, between the given and the grown, between the nature and the spirit. And in seeing it, I confirm my own freedom. I am free because I am outside the dream. I am free because I am in the state, even if I am a mistake in its allotment. The state is rational, and I am rational. Therefore, I am free. The dream is not. It is only a dream.
